item.text:
**8B.4 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed, 2024**

**Bottom Line**
Abiy **did** place some capable people and institutions into key execution roles, especially in **macro reform, central banking, finance, service delivery, and displacement policy**. But the record is **mixed**, because the security and political-control side still shows **loyalist consolidation, opaque coercive structures, and repression of watchdogs** rather than clean meritocratic empowerment.

**Positive / Capability-Enhancing Evidence**

- **House Approves Temesgen Tiruneh as Deputy Premier, Ambassador Taye Foreign Minister** — ENA English, 2024-02-08, [URL](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_3985658)  
  Claim: Abiy presented the nominees’ experience and the House unanimously approved Temesgen Tiruneh and Taye Atske Selassie. This supports a reading that at least some senior appointments were justified on competence grounds, not just patronage. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **Ethiopia names Mekdes Daba as health minister** — ENA English, 2024-02-08, [URL](https://www.ena.et/web/fre/w/fre_3987383)  
  Claim: the health portfolio was given to a minister publicly described in professional terms, supporting a technocratic staffing pattern in a core service ministry. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **Ethiopia’s Macro Reform Implementation** — ENA English, 2024-07-28, [URL](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4869646)  
  Claim: Abiy said Ethiopia had entered full implementation of macroeconomic reform to address debt burden, inflation, unemployment, and low productivity. This implies he empowered a reform team to execute a concrete program rather than leaving it abstract. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.1, 8B.2.

- **First Review under the Extended Credit Facility** — IMF, 2024-10-18, [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/10/18/pr-24383-ethiopia-imf-completes-the-1st-review-under-the-ecf-arrangement)  
  Claim: Ethiopia met all quantitative performance criteria and most structural benchmarks, which is strong evidence that the economic team was competent and empowered enough to deliver measurable compliance. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.1.

- **The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia: First Review Under the ECF Arrangement** — IMF, 2024, [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/11/04/the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-first-review-under-the-extended-credit-facility-557019)  
  Claim: the staff report says reforms were advancing, the exchange-rate transition was progressing, and the government had implemented most benchmarks. This supports the view that Abiy was backing a capable technocratic implementation team. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **The National Bank of Ethiopia Announces the Launch of a New Monetary Policy Framework** — National Bank of Ethiopia, 2024-07-09, [URL](https://nbe.gov.et/nbe_news/the-national-bank-of-ethiopia-announces-the-launch-of-a-new-monetary-policy-framework/)  
  Claim: the NBE said it had enhanced technical capacity, prioritized price stability, and moved to an interest-rate-based framework with new operating tools. This is direct evidence of empowering professional economic managers to execute reform. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **The Council of Ministers approved draft NBE and banking proclamations** — National Bank of Ethiopia, 2024-06-14, [URL](https://nbe.gov.et/nbe_news/the-council-of-ministers-today-approved-the-draft-nbe-proclamation-and-banking-business-proclamation/)  
  Claim: the draft laws were framed around credibility, accountability, transparency, and governance in the banking sector. That is strong evidence of institution-building and of selecting formal tools suited to capable execution. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **Energizing Ethiopia: New World Bank Program Expands Access to Electricity** — World Bank, 2024-04-03, [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/03/energizing-afe-ethiopia-new-world-bank-program-expands-access-to-electricity)  
  Claim: the government launched a phased power-sector reform plan to expand the grid, improve utility viability, and mobilize private participation. This suggests reliance on competent sector managers and implementers. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **Disclosable Restructuring Paper - Access to Distributed Electricity and Lighting in Ethiopia** — World Bank, 2024-08-16, [URL](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099082124120033234)  
  Claim: the project’s objective was to improve government capacity to mobilize and manage public financial and human resources, especially in administration, finance, procurement, and core systems. This is direct evidence of empowering administrative capability. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **Ethiopia launches inclusive ID system for refugees, boosts access to national services** — UNHCR Africa, 2024-03-07, [URL](https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/ethiopia-launches-inclusive-id-system-refugees-boosts-access-national-services)  
  Claim: the government, through RRS/NIDP and UNHCR, rolled out digital refugee IDs to improve access to services and formal permits. This supports a reading that Abiy empowered officials to run an inclusion-oriented administrative program. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **UN agencies and Ethiopian government launch Durable Solutions Strategy for internal displacement** — UNHCR, 2024-11-15, [URL](https://www.unhcr.org/news/announcements/un-agencies-and-ethiopian-government-launch-durable-solutions-strategy-internal)  
  Claim: Ethiopia and UN agencies launched a government-led strategy tying governance, social services, livelihoods, and peacebuilding to displacement solutions. That implies some capable coordination at the implementation level. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **ICRC Impact in Ethiopia: January - June 2024 Bulletin** — International Committee of the Red Cross, 2024-09-13, [URL](https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024)  
  Claim: the ICRC said it trained ENDF, police, militias, judges, and local authorities on IHL/IHRL. This is limited but real evidence that parts of the coercive apparatus were being brought under professional norms. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

**Negative / Loyalty- or Coercion-Enhancing Evidence**

- **Ethiopia intelligence head Temesgen approved as deputy prime minister** — Reuters via Yahoo News Canada, 2024-02-08, [URL](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ethiopia-intelligence-head-temesgen-approved-070230642.html)  
  Claim: Abiy moved the intelligence chief and ruling-party vice president into the deputy PM slot while shifting another security insider to NISS chief. That looks like consolidation of a security inner circle, not broad meritocratic empowerment. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.3.

- **The Reporter commentary on the reshuffle** — The Reporter, 2024-02-10, [URL](https://www.thereporterethiopia.com/38653/)  
  Claim: opposition voices argued the reshuffle was about consolidating loyalty rather than reform. This is weaker than Reuters, but it aligns with the pattern of security-centered staffing. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2.

- **Details of State of Emergency Declared by Gov't of Ethiopia** — ENA English, 2024-11-03, [URL](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124)  
  Claim: the proclamation centralized coercive authority under an operation command responsible to the prime minister and suspended ordinary judicial handling of enforcement. That is concrete evidence of coercive empowerment, not neutral professional staffing. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.3.

- **In Ethiopia, a secret committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels** — Reuters via EHRC, 2024-02-27, [URL](https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/)  
  Claim: the EHRC head confirmed Koree Nageenyaa existed and said it interfered in the justice system with widespread rights violations. This points to parallel coercive governance and politically shielded operators. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.3.

- **Freedom on the Net 2024: Ethiopia** — Freedom House, 2024, [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-net/2024)  
  Claim: authorities restricted internet access, used emergency powers against journalists, and deployed propaganda/manipulation tactics. That suggests state capacity was also being used to suppress scrutiny, not just to execute policy professionally. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.3.

- **Ethiopia: Authorities Suspend Three Rights Groups** — Human Rights Watch, 2024-12-02, [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups)  
  Claim: HRW said Abiy praised reform rhetoric while the government suspended rights groups and intensified crackdown. That is strong evidence of selective enforcement and loyalty discipline rather than empowering independent oversight. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.3.

- **Ethiopia’s Deepening Crackdown on Dissent** — Human Rights Watch, 2024-03-04, [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent)  
  Claim: arrests of opposition figures and journalists, plus disappearances and arbitrary detention, show that the security apparatus was mobilized heavily for repression rather than clean program execution. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.3.

- **Ethiopia authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent** — Amnesty International, 2024-02-19, [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/)  
  Claim: emergency powers were used for warrantless arrests, curfews, movement limits, and bans on assemblies. This shows mobilization of state force for coercive control rather than narrowly professional administration. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.3.

- **Ethiopia: authorities suspend three rights groups** — Human Rights Watch, 2024-12-02, [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups)  
  Claim: the government kept punishing civic actors even while praising reforms, indicating selective use of state power and loyalty enforcement rather than neutral appointment of capable monitors. IDs: 8B.4; also 8B.2, 8B.3.

**Search Gap**

I found **good evidence in the economic and administrative sphere** that Abiy empowered competent officials and institutions. I found **much weaker evidence** of broad meritocratic staffing in the security sphere, where the pattern instead points to **inner-circle consolidation, secret committees, and coercive enforcement**. I did **not** find a single 2024 source showing a comprehensive across-the-board merit-based staffing standard; the evidence is sectoral, not uniform.
